prompt: In Cloud Run and Azure Container Apps, every deploy automatically creates a new, immutable, independently-addressable unit that live traffic can be instantly routed back to. What is this unit called on both platforms?
choices: A task definition
A stack
A revision
A deployment manifest

prompt: On ECS Fargate, which object defines a task's CPU, memory, port mappings, and environment variables, and becomes a new immutable numbered revision every time it changes?
choices: The cluster
The task definition
The service
The target group

prompt: An image is already deployed and live. You need to change a non-secret runtime config value (like an external API base URL) without changing application code. What is the correct way to do this on Cloud Run?
choices: Edit the Dockerfile ENV instruction and rebuild the image
SSH into the running container and edit the value in place
Change the value in the CI/CD pipeline YAML and wait for the next scheduled build
Run `gcloud run services update --update-env-vars` to create a new revision from the same image

prompt: Following the never-commit-state principle first introduced with Terraform state and .tfvars files, where should an actual secret value (like a database password) live when it needs to be injected into a deployed container?
choices: As a literal value passed to --set-env-vars in a deploy script committed to the repo
Hardcoded as a Dockerfile ENV instruction
In a secrets manager (Secret Manager / SSM Parameter Store / Key Vault), referenced by name at deploy time
In the task definition JSON's environment array, committed to git

prompt: A bad deploy to Cloud Run is causing 500 errors on the latest revision. The previous revision orders-api-00042-xyz is known-good. What is the fastest correct way to revert live traffic?
choices: Delete the bad revision's image from the container registry
Run `gcloud run services update-traffic orders-api --to-revisions=orders-api-00042-xyz=100`
Run `git revert` on the last commit and wait for CI to rebuild and redeploy
Scale the service to zero instances and then back up

prompt: On ECS Fargate, task definitions are immutable: updating one creates a new numbered revision rather than changing it in place. What command rolls a running service back to a previous task definition revision?
choices: `aws ecs deregister-task-definition --revision 41`
`aws ecr batch-delete-image --repository-name orders-api`
`aws ecs update-service --cluster orders-cluster --service orders-api-svc --task-definition orders-api:41 --force-new-deployment`
`aws ecs stop-task --task-definition orders-api:41`

prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts what you must configure on each platform to deploy a container?
choices: All three require you to provision and patch your own virtual machines
ECS Fargate has no concept of a cluster or task definition
Azure Container Apps requires manually wiring a load balancer and target group for every app, same as ECS

Cloud Run configures a managed service directly from an image; ECS Fargate requires a separately defined cluster, task definition, and service; Azure Container Apps requires a shared Container Apps Environment plus the container app itself

prompt: Why does scaling-to-zero matter when planning a Cloud Run rollback?
choices: Rollback is only possible while min-instances is set to 0
If the previous good revision has scaled to zero, the first request after rollback pays a cold-start cost while a new instance spins up
Scaling to zero permanently deletes old revisions, making rollback impossible
Cloud Run refuses to route traffic to any revision that has scaled to zero
